title: Reflection on whether Chat GPT should be banned by academia from the perspective of education and teaching
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the debate over whether ChatGPT should be banned in academia, focusing on its implications for education, teaching, and academic integrity. Rather than reporting an empirical study, it offers an opinion-based analysis of the opportunities and risks posed by generative AI in educational settings.

The paper argues that ChatGPT and similar AI tools can support learning, teaching, and educational digital transformation by enabling personalized tutoring, more efficient information retrieval, automated text generation, and new forms of student inquiry. It discusses potential uses in school and higher education contexts, including classroom support, assessment, and broader educational reform, while also acknowledging concerns about cheating, over-reliance, privacy, bias, and ethical misuse.

The discussion is framed around students, teachers, schools, universities, and education policymakers, with examples drawn largely from K-12 and higher education policy responses in multiple countries. The author concludes that outright bans are not advisable; instead, AI tools should be regulated, integrated responsibly into education, and paired with updated teaching methods, assessment practices, and governance to protect academic integrity while leveraging their benefits.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a 2023 opinion/reflection article with no original empirical study design, no comparison group, and no measured outcomes. It is peer-reviewed but does not provide methodological evidence for causal claims.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper discusses potentially important system-level and skill-related implications of ChatGPT for education, but it reports no empirical effects or effect sizes. The impact is therefore plausible but unclear rather than demonstrated.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT as a general-purpose educational assistant for student question answering, personalized tutoring, writing support, and teacher assistance in K-12 and higher education contexts

finding.finding_summary: This is a conceptual opinion paper, not an empirical evaluation, so it does not report measured effects on outcomes. The paper argues that ChatGPT may improve educational digital transformation and efficiency, but also raises concerns about academic integrity, privacy, and governance, with no sample size or effect size reported.
finding.measure: policy and governance discussion; no empirical outcome measure

finding.finding_summary: The paper argues that ChatGPT could support critical thinking, problem solving, creativity, and self-directed learning if used appropriately, but may also weaken independent thinking and judgment through over-reliance. These claims are theoretical and not backed by experimental data in the paper.
finding.measure: theoretical discussion of critical thinking, independent thinking, and problem-solving
